```
    Safari: 17.5
  npmPackages:
    react: ^18.3.1 => 18.3.1
    typescript: 5.1.6 => 5.1.6
```

### Describe the bug

I have a plugin that looks sort of like this:

```typescript
const OutputData = z
  .object({
    some: z.string(),
  });

const pluginT = initTRPC.create();

const pluginProc = pluginT.procedure.output(OutputData).use(async (opts) =>
  opts.next({
    ctx: {
      additional: "context",
    },
  }),
);
```

Which I then use like this:

```typescript
protectedUserProcedure
  .unstable_concat(pluginProc)
  .input(z.object({
    some: z.number(),
  }))
  .output(z.object({
    regular: z.literal("output"),
  }))
  .query(...)
```

But this throws:

```
 ⨯ Error: Duplicate key output
    at mergeWithoutOverrides (webpack-internal:///(api)/../../node_modules/.pnpm/@trpc+server@11.0.0-rc.374/node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/unstable-core-do-not-import/utils.mjs:19:23)
    at createNewBuilder (webpack-internal:///(api)/../../node_modules/.pnpm/@trpc+server@11.0.0-rc.374/node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/unstable-core-do-not-import/procedureBuilder.mjs:18:77)
    at Object.output (webpack-internal:///(api)/../../node_modules/.pnpm/@trpc+server@11.0.0-rc.374/node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/unstable-core-do-not-import/procedureBuilder.mjs:55:20)
    at eval (webpack-internal:///(api)/../../packages/backend/src/trpc/routes/myRoute.ts:60:9)
```

### Link to reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-svr83h

The starter repo is broken for me, but it should do the trick.

items.title: feat(server): add per-procedure error formatters with .errors()
items.body:
Closes #6832 #3438

## 🎯 Changes

* Adds `.errors()` to the procedure builder, so a procedure can declare the errors *it* can throw without every other procedure having to know about them.
* No breaking changes — routers that don't call `.errors()` behave exactly as before.
* Errors bubble until either a `.errors()` formatter handles them or they hit the global error formatter
* formatted errors are treated like an errorFormatter result and returned to the client
* `.input()`/`.output()` errors may also be handled by `.errors()`  
* may be chained
* docs: https://33fa1ur95-kaghb7ptn-trpc.vercel.app/docs/server/error-formatting#per-procedure-error-formatting

```ts
const rateLimitedProcedure = t.procedure
  .errors((opts) => {
    if (opts.error.cause instanceof RateLimitError) {
      return {
        ...opts.shape,
        data: { ...opts.shape.data, kind: 'RATE_LIMIT' as const, retryAfterMs: opts.error.cause.retryAfterMs },
      };
    }
    return undefined; // decline
  })
  .use(rateLimiterMiddleware())
  .errors((opts) => {
    // some other error formatting
  })
  .query(() => /* some logic */);
```
## ✅ Checklist

- [x] If necessary, I have added documentation related to the changes made.
- [x] I have added or updated the tests related to the changes made.

- **New Features**
  - Added procedure-level error formatting through `.errors()`, allowing individual procedures to provide custom error details.
  - Added support for chaining formatters, fallback to global formatting, and consistent handling across queries, mutations, subscriptions, HTTP, and WebSocket connections.
  - Procedure-specific error shapes are now reflected in client-side type information.
  - Exported utilities for inferring procedure error shapes.

- **Documentation**
  - Added guidance and examples for procedure-level error formatting, including rate-limit and payment scenarios.

    @trpc/client: 11.0.0-rc.833 => 11.0.0-rc.833+16e52ebcf 
    @trpc/react-query: 11.0.0-rc.833 => 11.0.0-rc.833+16e52ebcf

    react: 18.3.1 => 18.3.1 
    typescript: ^5.7.3 => 5.7.3 

### Describe the bug

When using unstable concat. Some of the input type's data get's weird. For example, when using z.number().default(), as input validation, the input provided to the query should be a number. However, after passing through a unstable_concat, it will be number or undefined.

### Link to reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-1raqfonu?file=src%2Fserver%2Ftrpc.ts

### To reproduce

If you hover over the input on the without_unstable_concat, it will show that the input is a number.
However, if you hover over the input on the with_unstable_concat, it will show that the input is a number or undefined
